q: What comes next? 🦈 🐟 🦈 🐟 🦈 ❓
why: The pattern is shark, fish, shark, fish. After a shark comes a fish.
hint: Say the pattern out loud. Which two repeat?

q: Bat, mitt and snorkel: which one is NOT used to play baseball?
why: A bat hits the ball and a mitt catches it. A snorkel is for swimming.
hint: Think about what players use on the field.

q: 🪐 ⭐ 🪐 ⭐ 🪐 ⭐ 🪐 ⭐  How many ⭐ are in the row?
why: Count only the stars. They sit between the planets: 1, 2, 3, 4.
hint: Touch each ⭐ and count. Skip the 🪐.

q: What comes next? 🔴 🔴 🟦 🔴 🔴 ❓
why: The pattern is two reds, then one blue. We just had two reds, so blue is next.
hint: Look for the group that keeps repeating.

q: Put these sea animals in order from smallest to biggest.
why: A shrimp fits in your hand. A turtle is bigger, a great white is bigger still, and a blue whale is giant.
hint: Start with the one you could hold.

q: Counting by 2s should go 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Here is a row: 2, 4, 6, 7, 10. Which number is a mistake?
why: After 6 we add 2 and get 8, not 7. The 7 broke the pattern.
hint: Add 2 each time and see where it goes wrong.

q: True or false: after 🔺 🔵 🔺 🔵 🔺 🔵 the next shape is 🔺.
why: The pattern is triangle, circle, triangle, circle. The row ended on a circle, so a triangle is next.
hint: See which shape the row ended on.

q: A baseball team has 9 players on the field. 3 of them are in the outfield. How many are NOT in the outfield?
why: 9 take away 3 leaves 6 players. They are the pitcher, catcher and infielders.
hint: Start at 9 and count back 3.

q: Put a baby dinosaur's life in order, first to last.
why: Dinosaurs started in an egg. They hatched, grew up, and then could lay eggs of their own.
hint: What comes before hatching?

q: 🦈 🦈 🦈 🐬 🦈  Which place is the odd one out?
why: Four animals are sharks and one is a dolphin. The dolphin is in the 4th spot.
hint: Find the one that is different, then count from the left.

q: A rocket countdown goes 5, 4, 3, ❓, 1. What number is missing?
why: Count backward by 1 each time. After 3 comes 2, and then 1.
hint: Count backward one step at a time.

q: A whale is bigger than a crab. A crab is bigger than a shrimp. Which one is the smallest?
why: The shrimp is smaller than the crab, and the crab is smaller than the whale. So shrimp is smallest.
hint: Line them up from big to small.

q: A rocket counts down by 2s: 30, 28, 26, 24, ❓. What number comes next?
why: Each number is 2 less than the one before. 24 minus 2 is 22.
hint: Find how much each number drops.

q: A dino dig numbers its bones: 3, 8, 13, 18, ❓. What number comes next?
why: The numbers go up by 5 each time. 18 plus 5 is 23.
hint: Subtract neighbors to find the jump.

q: Shark A shows 15 teeth. Shark B shows 51 teeth. Which shark shows MORE teeth?
why: 51 has 5 tens and 15 has only 1 ten. The tens digit decides.
hint: Compare the tens digits first.

q: Home runs hit by four players: 18, 9, 31, 24. Put them from fewest to most.
why: Compare the tens first: 9 is the smallest, then 18, then 24, then 31.
hint: Find the smallest first, then the next.

q: The fins box holds a shark, a tuna and an eagle. Which one is in the wrong box?
why: Sharks and tuna are fish with fins. An eagle has wings, so it belongs in a different box.
hint: Ask which animal has no fins.

q: A star pattern grows: group 1 has 1 star, group 2 has 3 stars, group 3 has 5 stars. How many stars are in group 5?
why: Each group adds 2 stars: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Group 5 has 9 stars.
hint: Find how many stars each group adds.

q: The even box holds 4, 8 and 12. Which number also belongs in the even box?
why: Even numbers split into two equal groups. 18 does, but 15 and 21 leave one extra.
hint: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.

q: Sam throws faster than Lee. Lee throws faster than Ty. Put the pitchers from slowest to fastest.
why: Ty is slower than Lee and Lee is slower than Sam. So the order is Ty, Lee, Sam.
hint: Find who is slower than everyone.

q: Four of these numbers are even and one is not: 12, 14, 16, 19, 20. Which does NOT belong?
why: 12, 14, 16 and 20 are all even. 19 is odd, so it is the one left out.
hint: Check the last digit of each number.

q: True or false: if you count by 5s from 5 (5, 10, 15, 20...), you will say the number 18.
why: Counting by 5s lands on numbers ending in 5 or 0. 18 ends in 8, so you skip it.
hint: Look at the last digit each time.

q: The Rangers scored 6 runs. The Waves scored 4 more runs than the Rangers. How many runs did the Waves score?
why: 4 more than 6 is 10. The Waves scored 10 runs.
hint: Start at 6 and count up 4.

q: Which shape goes in the empty spot? Row 1: 🔺 🔷 🔺. Row 2: 🔷 🔺 🔷. Row 3: 🔺 🔷 ❓
why: Every row and column swaps between triangle and diamond. After 🔺 🔷 comes 🔺.
hint: Look at what is above the empty spot.

q: A moon rover finds this many rocks each day: 2, 5, 8, 11. If the pattern keeps going, how many on day 5?
why: The pattern adds 3 each day. 11 plus 3 is 14.
hint: Check how much it grows from day to day.

q: Jo is taller than Kai. Lee is shorter than Kai. Mo is taller than Jo. Put the four players from shortest to tallest.
why: Lee is below Kai, Kai is below Jo, and Jo is below Mo. Chain them together.
hint: Draw a line and place one player at a time.

q: A fossil hunter's boxes hold 4, 7, 10, 13 bones, and so on. How many bones are in the 7th box?
why: Each box holds 3 more. After 13 comes 16, 19, then 22 in the 7th box.
hint: Keep adding the same number, box by box.

q: Each row and column has one 🦈, one 🐙 and one 🐢. Row 1: 🦈 🐙 🐢. Row 2: 🐙 🐢 🦈. Row 3: 🐢 ❓ 🐙. What goes in ❓?
why: Row 3 already has 🐢 and 🐙, so it needs 🦈. Column 2 agrees.
hint: Which animal is missing from Row 3?

q: The pattern 🪐 ⭐ ⭐ repeats over and over. Among the first 10 items, how many are ⭐?
why: Items 1 to 10 are 🪐⭐⭐ 🪐⭐⭐ 🪐⭐⭐ 🪐. That is three groups of 2 stars.
hint: Write out all 10 items and count.

q: In a dino parade, Stegosaurus walks behind Triceratops. T. rex walks in front of Triceratops. Who walks last?
why: The line is T. rex, Triceratops, Stegosaurus. The one behind everybody is last.
hint: Put the three dinos in a line.

q: True or false: in the pattern 20, 17, 14, 11, the next number is 8.
why: Each number is 3 less than the one before. 11 minus 3 is 8.
hint: Find how much each number drops.

q: Work out each sum, then put them from least to greatest.
why: The sums are 8, 10, 11 and 13. Order the answers, not the first numbers.
hint: Add first, then compare the answers.

q: A skip pattern goes 6, 9, 12, 16, 18. Which number is the mistake?
why: Adding 3 each time gives 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. The 16 should be 15.
hint: Add the same jump each time to find the break.

q: In each row of a number grid, the three numbers add up to 12. Row 1: 5, 4, 3. Row 2: 6, ❓, 2. What number is ❓?
why: 6 plus 2 is 8. To reach 12 you need 4 more.
hint: First add the two numbers you can see.

q: Three of these are sharks. Which one is NOT a shark?
why: Hammerheads, great whites and whale sharks are fish. An orca is really a dolphin, a mammal that breathes air.
hint: Think about which are fish and which breathe air.

q: The letters follow a pattern: A B A C A D A ❓. What comes next?
why: Every other letter is A. The letters in between go B, C, D, so E is next.
hint: Look at the letters between the A's.

q: Mystery number: it is more than 20, less than 30, a multiple of 7, and odd. What is it?
why: The multiples of 7 between 20 and 30 are 21 and 28. Only 21 is odd.
hint: List the multiples of 7 near 20 first.

q: A pitcher's jersey number has two digits. The digits add up to 9, and the tens digit is double the ones digit. What is the number?
why: Try 6 and 3. They add to 9, and 6 is double 3. So the number is 63.
hint: Try pairs of digits that add to 9.

q: Every shark in an aquarium is gray. Mia sees a gray fish and says it must be a shark. What is wrong with her thinking?
opts: Other kinds of fish can be gray too
why: The clue says sharks are gray, not that every gray fish is a shark.
hint: Does the clue work backward too?

q: Leo has 3 boxes with 4 stickers in each. He says 3 + 4 = 7 stickers. How many stickers does he really have?
why: Each box has 4, and there are 3 boxes: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. He added the wrong numbers.
hint: Add the stickers box by box.

q: Nia, Omar and Pia each love a different thing: sharks, dinosaurs or space. Nia loves neither sharks nor dinosaurs. Omar does not love sharks. Who loves sharks?
why: Nia must love space. Omar does not love sharks, so he loves dinosaurs. That leaves Pia with sharks.
hint: Start with the kid who has the most clues.

q: Four dinosaurs race. Yan finishes right after Zed. Wes finishes before Zed. Xia finishes after Yan. Put them in finishing order, first to last.
why: Wes comes before Zed, Yan is right after Zed, and Xia is after Yan. That makes Wes, Zed, Yan, Xia.
hint: Place the one with a 'before' clue first.

q: A crab walks from A to B, moving only right or down. B is 2 steps right and 2 steps down from A. How many different shortest paths can it take?
why: List them: RRDD, RDRD, RDDR, DRRD, DRDR, DDRR. That is 6 paths.
hint: List the paths in an organized way.

q: True or false: All sharks are fish, and a hammerhead is a shark. So a hammerhead must be a fish.
why: A hammerhead is a shark, and every shark is a fish. So the conclusion must be true.
hint: Follow the chain one link at a time.

q: Which number fits ALL the clues? It is between 40 and 60. It is a multiple of 5. The tens digit is 5. The ones digit is odd.
why: Multiples of 5 with a tens digit of 5 are 50 and 55. Only 55 has an odd ones digit.
hint: Cross out numbers one clue at a time.

q: Four fans leave a baseball game after 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4 of it is done. Put them from the first to leave to the last.
why: Eighths are the smallest pieces, then fourths, then halves. 3/4 is the biggest, so that fan leaves last.
hint: Picture a pizza cut into pieces.

q: Today is Wednesday. A rocket launches in 10 days. What day of the week is the launch?
why: 7 days later is Wednesday again, and 3 more days is Saturday.
hint: Count a full week first, then the extra days.

q: A coach says: 'We lost our last 3 games, so we will lose the next one.' What is wrong with that thinking?
opts: Teams cannot lose 3 in a row
He should say they will win
Past games do not decide the next one
why: The next game is a new game. Earlier losses cannot force a result.
hint: Does the past control what happens next?

q: If it rains, the baseball game is canceled. The game was NOT canceled. What must be true?
why: If rain always cancels the game, then no cancellation means there was no rain.
hint: Test it: what would rain have done to the game?

q: A toy shark balances 3 toy fish on a scale. One toy fish balances 2 toy crabs. How many toy crabs balance one toy shark?
why: One shark equals 3 fish. Each fish equals 2 crabs. So 3 groups of 2 make 6 crabs.
hint: Turn the shark into fish first.

q: Moon rocks on a balance scale: A is heavier than B. C is lighter than B. D is heavier than A. Order them from lightest to heaviest.
why: C is below B, B is below A, and A is below D. Chain the clues together.
hint: Build a line one clue at a time.

q: What number comes next in this pattern? 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 15, ❓
why: The steps take turns: add 1, then double. 15 doubled is 30.
hint: Two different steps take turns.

q: A fossil hunter doubled her bones, then found 5 more. Now she has 21 bones. How many did she start with?
why: Work backward: 21 minus 5 is 16. Half of 16 is 8.
hint: Undo the steps in reverse order.

q: If it rains, the game is canceled. The game was canceled. Did it rain?
why: Rain causes cancellation, but other things could cancel a game too, such as lightning or a broken field.
hint: Could anything else cancel a game?

q: In a class of 20 kids, 12 like sharks and 10 like dinosaurs. Every kid likes at least one. How many like both?
why: 12 + 10 = 22, which is 2 more than 20 kids. Those 2 were counted twice.
hint: Add the groups, then compare with the class size.

q: A toy starfish and 2 marbles balance 5 marbles on a scale. How many marbles balance one toy starfish?
why: Take 2 marbles from each side. The starfish balances the 3 marbles left.
hint: Remove the same thing from both sides.

q: True or false: If a shape is a square, it has 4 sides. This shape has 4 sides, so it must be a square.
why: Rectangles and diamonds have 4 sides too. Square leads to 4 sides, but 4 sides does not lead to square.
hint: Can you draw a 4-sided shape that is not a square?

q: A pattern grows: ⚾ 🧢 ⚾⚾ 🧢 ⚾⚾⚾ 🧢 and so on. Counting from 1, in which spot is the 5th 🧢?
why: Caps sit after groups of 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 balls. That is 15 balls and 5 caps, so spot 20.
hint: Keep writing the pattern out and count each spot.

q: Sam thinks of a number, adds 6, then halves the result. He gets 7. What was his number?
why: Undo halving: 7 doubled is 14. Undo adding 6: 14 minus 6 is 8.
hint: Undo the last step first.

q: A space show ended at 4:10 PM after running 2 hours and 25 minutes. When did it start?
why: Back up 2 hours to 2:10. Then back up 25 minutes to 1:45 PM.
hint: Go back one hour piece, then the minutes.

q: A toy bat and a toy ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1 more than the ball. How many cents does the ball cost?
why: Try 5 cents: the bat is $1.05 and the total is $1.10. A 10-cent ball makes the total $1.20.
hint: Test your first guess by adding both prices.

q: Two coins add up to 30 cents. One of them is not a nickel. Which two coins are they?
why: The quarter is the one that is not a nickel. The other coin IS a nickel. 25 + 5 = 30.
hint: Read 'one of them' very carefully.

q: Finn and Gill are sharks in a riddle. Each always tells the truth or always lies. Finn says: 'At least one of us is a liar.' Who is who?
opts: Finn lies and Gill tells the truth
Finn tells the truth and Gill lies
why: If Finn were a liar, his sentence would be true. That is impossible. So Finn is honest, and Gill is the liar.
hint: Test what happens if Finn is a liar.

q: 6 baseball players shake hands after a game. Every player shakes hands with every other player exactly once. How many handshakes happen?
why: Each of 6 players shakes 5 hands, which counts every handshake twice: 30 divided by 2 is 15.
hint: Count one player's handshakes, then fix the double counting.

q: A cube net has four squares in a row: A, B, C, D. Square E is above B and square F is below B. Folded into a cube, which square is opposite B?
why: A, B, C, D wrap around the cube like a belt. Squares two steps apart are opposite, so D faces B.
hint: Picture the row of four wrapping around a box.

q: Five players bat in order. Rae bats last. Sol bats right before Rae. Pat bats before Quinn. Tia bats before Pat. Put them in batting order, first to last.
why: Rae is 5th and Sol is 4th. Tia, Pat, Quinn fill spots 1 to 3, with Tia before Pat before Quinn.
hint: Place the sure spots first, then fill the gaps.

q: A 3 by 3 by 3 cube is painted red on the outside, then cut into 27 small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly 2 red faces?
why: Those are the edge cubes, one in the middle of each of the 12 edges. Corners show 3 red faces.
hint: Where do two painted faces meet?

q: A museum has 17 dinosaur skeletons. All but 9 of them are moved to a new hall. How many skeletons did NOT move?
why: 'All but 9' means 9 stayed behind. The other 8 moved. The 17 is a distraction.
hint: Which ones did NOT move?

q: Algae in a tide pool doubles every day. On day 12 it covers the whole pool. On which day was the pool half covered?
why: One doubling later it fills the pool. So half-covered was one day earlier, on day 11.
hint: Doubling goes forward. What does half do backward?

q: A dark drawer holds 10 red baseball socks and 10 blue ones, all mixed up. What is the fewest socks you must grab to be SURE of a matching pair?
why: Two socks might be one of each color. The third sock must match one of the first two.
hint: What is the worst luck you could have?

q: True or false: A fair coin lands heads 5 times in a row. On the next flip, tails is more likely.
why: Each flip is separate. The coin does not remember, so heads and tails are still equally likely.
hint: Does a coin remember its past flips?

q: 8 space rocks look identical, but one is heavier. What is the fewest weighings on a balance scale that is guaranteed to find the heavy one?
why: Weigh 3 against 3. Balanced means it's in the other 2; otherwise it's in the heavier 3. One more weighing finishes.
hint: One weighing has 3 outcomes: left, right, balanced.
